appraisal_events.evidence: she affects the jargon of studios and coteries in an irritating way, using Robert's own borrowed expressions as if they were a necessary language; and the narrator later notes he was to see her, an hour afterward, showing great deference toward the very artists she had judged so severely.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator undercuts Rachel's genuine wit and culture by exposing her affected jargon and, more decisively, by revealing that her ironic superiority toward famous artists is contradicted by her private deference to those same artists, framing her critical stance as hollow performance.

appraisal_events.evidence: — Zézette, je te prierai de ne pas regarder ce jeune homme comme cela ... si tu dois nous donner en spectacle, j'aime mieux déjeuner de mon côté et aller t'attendre au théâtre. Saint-Loup's face reddens into a «nuée sanglante» as he speaks.
appraisal_events.explanation: After Rachel makes eyes at a young stranger, Saint-Loup publicly reprimands her, his blush and distended features registering real jealousy and distress; the narrator's sympathetic description of his friend's reaction frames the rebuke as justified.

status_effects.explanation: Rachel's critical persona is locally diminished when the narrator shows her scorn for established artists to be a pose belied by her actual deference to them.
Rachel is publicly checked and put in her place by Saint-Loup, who threatens to leave her if she persists, asserting control over her conduct in front of others.
Saint-Loup's composure visibly breaks down into a jealous, reddening outburst in front of the group, showing him at the mercy of Rachel's behavior.

ambiguities: The text hedges Rachel's motive for flirting with the young stockbroker ('peut-être pour faire partir Robert afin de se trouver seule avec Aimé'), leaving uncertain whether the provocation targeted the stranger or was a pretext connected to Aimé; this does not change the blame event's target (Rachel) but qualifies how deliberate her provocation is read to be.
